about: A 20 to 40 second launch film made from a product's own site, the launch pictures, and a check for any video.

tools.name: make_launch_film
tools.title: Launch film from a website
tools.asks: a launch video, product video, promo, teaser or announcement clip for a product's site or app
tools.description: Makes a {fact:launch-film.length_min} to {fact:launch-film.length_max} second launch film from a product's own site in one job: it reads the brand and the page, plans the film (name and promise, the real screen in a browser window, the page's own headline, feature cards, a number the page states when it finds one, the logo close) and renders film.mp4 with music and sound effects, with Chrome and ffmpeg on this machine. Nothing is generated by AI: the film shows what the site says. The result shows film.json, the plan, next to words.json, the page's words, and frames/sheet.jpg has two stills a clip. The film is {fact:launch-film.fps} frames a second at {fact:launch-film.size_16_9} or {fact:launch-film.size_9_16}, its sound about {fact:launch-film.lufs} LUFS. Its music is the look's own: film.json takes no track, so for the user's own track plan with music false and lay the track in afterwards. For a plan to read or change before it renders, use plan_launch_film instead. The address needs a dot in its host, so localhost is refused.
tools.hostedDescription: Makes a {fact:launch-film.length_min} to {fact:launch-film.length_max} second launch film from a product's own site in one job: it reads the brand and the page, plans the film (name and promise, the real screen in a browser window, the page's own headline, feature cards, a number the page states when it finds one, the logo close) and renders film.mp4 with music and sound effects. Nothing is generated by AI: the film shows what the site says. The result shows film.json, the plan, next to words.json, the page's words. A film.json cannot be changed here yet, so it renders as it was planned, and render_launch_film renders it again from job:<job_id>/film.json. The film is {fact:launch-film.fps} frames a second at {fact:launch-film.size_16_9} or {fact:launch-film.size_9_16}, its sound about {fact:launch-film.lufs} LUFS. Its music is the look's own, and no track of the user's can go into it here. For a plan to read before it renders, use plan_launch_film instead. The address needs a dot in its host.

url.description: The product's website, like https://linear.app, or its App Store or Google Play listing. A social profile is refused, and so is a host without a dot, like localhost.

look.description: The film's look, which also sets the tempo of its music and so how long a bar lasts (default: picked from the brand). launch_film_guide with topic looks says what each one suits.

seconds.description: Aim for this length (default {default:make_launch_film.seconds}). Clips last whole bars of the look's music and the plan never stretches one to fill the time, so the film can end several seconds away from it, often short; film.timeline.json has its exact length.

aspect.description: 16:9 (default) or 9:16 for phones. For both, make the second one with words from the first.

brand.description: A brand kit you already have: its folder or its brand.json. make_brand_kit makes one. The kit copies the kit given into brand/ in the film's folder; without one, it reads the brand from the site itself.
brand.hostedDescription: A brand kit an earlier job saved, as job:<job_id>/brand.json, so its logo files come with it. make_brand_kit makes one. The kit copies the kit given into the film's brand/ folder; without one, it reads the brand from the site itself.

words.description: A words.json from an earlier plan or film, used instead of reading the page again, so a second aspect keeps the same words.

music.description: Set to false to leave out the look's music bed, as when the user's own track goes under the film later.

sfx.description: Set to false to leave out the sound effects.

jobs.description: Clips rendered at once (default {default:make_launch_film.jobs}). 1 suits a slow machine.

keep.description: Keep the work files, each clip's MP4, in a launch-film-work- folder in the system's temp folder, outside the film's folder; the summary names it.

refuses: is not a command or an address

done: Check the brand's name and every word on screen in film.json below against words.json and the site, and look at {file:frames/sheet.jpg}, or give the user its path, before handing the film over.
Then call check_video with film {file:film.mp4} and expect {fact:launch-film.size_16_9}@{fact:launch-film.fps}, or {fact:launch-film.size_9_16}@{fact:launch-film.fps} for 9:16.
To change a word, change it in {file:film.json} and call render_launch_film with film {file:film.json}.
failed: makersmcp_playbook {topic} lists this tool's errors and their fixes.

When the reason shows "Planned <n> clips", or a clip it rendered, this run replaced film.json, words.json and brand/ in {folder}, so the film.mp4, film.timeline.json and frames/ there may be of the earlier film: make the film again before using them.
A run that failed while reading the site, before it planned, may have emptied or replaced {folder}/brand, which an earlier film.json there needs, so plan again before rendering one.

done: Check the brand's name and every word on screen in film.json below against words.json and the site: a film.json cannot be changed here, so when one is wrong, tell the user instead of rendering it again.
Then call check_video with film {file:film.mp4} and expect {fact:launch-film.size_16_9}@{fact:launch-film.fps}, or {fact:launch-film.size_9_16}@{fact:launch-film.fps} for 9:16.
Give the user the {name:frames/sheet.jpg} link from the list below: two stills a clip.
Give the user the {name:film.mp4} link from the list below to watch before it goes out.
failed: makersmcp_playbook {topic} lists this tool's errors and their fixes.

When the reason says the brand could not be read, no tool here takes a logo file or colors, and a brand kit of the same site stops the same way: ask for the product's own site when the address is not it, or for an app its App Store listing.

tools.title: Plan a launch film
tools.asks: to choose a launch film's look, length or words, or to read its plan before it renders
tools.description: Reads a product's brand and page and writes film.json, the plan of a launch film, without rendering it. The result shows film.json, words.json (the page's words) and brand/BRAND.md, so every word on screen can be checked against the page before the render. Change film.json where it is wrong (launch_film_guide with topic types lists the scene types), then render it with render_launch_film. A second aspect is a second plan with words from the first and the other aspect. For a film in one job, use make_launch_film instead.

tools.name: render_launch_film
tools.title: Render a launch film
tools.asks: a film.json rendered into film.mp4, after a plan or a change
tools.description: Renders a film.json into film.mp4 next to it, with Chrome and ffmpeg on this machine, and writes film.timeline.json, each clip's start and length, which the result shows. It replaces the film.mp4 and film.timeline.json of an earlier render there and does not draw frames/ again. check_video makes a new sheet.png to look at. The film is {fact:launch-film.fps} frames a second. Rendering a 30 second film takes {fact:launch-film.render_minutes}.
tools.hostedDescription: Renders the film.json of an earlier make_launch_film or plan_launch_film job into film.mp4, as it was planned, and writes film.timeline.json, each clip's start and length, which the result shows. The film is {fact:launch-film.fps} frames a second. Rendering a 30 second film takes {fact:launch-film.render_minutes}.

film.description: The film.json to render. film.mp4 and film.timeline.json go next to it.
film.hostedDescription: The film.json an earlier job saved, as job:<job_id>/film.json, so the brand and screens it names come with it.

jobs.description: Clips rendered at once (default {default:render_launch_film.jobs}). 1 suits a slow machine.

keep.description: Keep the work files, each clip's MP4, in a launch-film-work- folder in the system's temp folder, outside the film's folder; the summary names it.

tools.name: make_launch_stills
tools.title: Launch pictures
tools.asks: Product Hunt gallery images and thumbnail, an og:image, an X post image, a Google Play feature graphic or Chrome Web Store tiles
tools.description: Makes the pictures a launch needs at the exact size each place asks for, as opaque PNGs in stills/, listed in STILLS.md, which the result shows. ph makes ph-1.png (the logo, the promise and the screen) and up to {fact:launch-film.ph_frames_max} of the film's scenes from ph-2.png on, all {fact:launch-film.still_size.ph}, and ph-thumbnail.png at {fact:launch-film.still_size.ph_thumbnail}; og makes og.png at {fact:launch-film.still_size.og}; x makes x.png at {fact:launch-film.still_size.x}; play makes play-feature.png at {fact:launch-film.still_size.play}, Google Play's feature graphic only; chrome makes chrome-small.png at {fact:launch-film.still_size.chrome_small} and chrome-marquee.png at {fact:launch-film.still_size.chrome_marquee}. The words and the look come from a film.json, the logo from the brand and the screen from the site; no picture is 9:16. Given a site instead of a film.json, it plans a film first with the default look, length and aspect. For App Store or Google Play screenshots, use take_screenshots instead.

source.description: The product's website, like https://linear.app, or a film.json you already have, so the pictures match that film. Given the website, it plans a film first with the default look, length and aspect; stills/ goes next to the film.json. The address needs a dot in its host, so localhost is refused.
source.hostedDescription: The product's website, like https://linear.app, or the film.json an earlier job saved, as job:<job_id>/film.json, so the pictures match that film. The address needs a dot in its host. A link is read as the website, and one that ends in .json is refused.

for.description: Which places to make pictures for (default all of them): ph, the Product Hunt gallery and thumbnail; og, a link preview; x, a post on X; play, the Google Play feature graphic; chrome, the Chrome Web Store tiles.

done: Read STILLS.md below and look at every picture, or give the user the paths to look at, then tell the user which place each file is for and its size.

To change their words, change them in {file:film.json} and make the pictures again with source {file:film.json} and every place in for, since a run leaves the pictures of the other places as they were.
To change their words, change them in {input:source} and make the pictures again with source {input:source} and every place in for, since a run leaves the pictures of the other places as they were.
Tell the user which place each picture is for and its size, from STILLS.md below, with the links from the list.

tools.name: check_video
tools.title: Check a video
tools.asks: a video checked before it goes out: size, frame rate, length, loudness, blank or frozen stretches, cuts on the beat
tools.description: Checks any video by measuring it with ffmpeg: size, frame rate, length, black, still and silent stretches, loudness, true peak, clipping, and whether the cuts land on the beat. It writes CHECK.md (pass or fail, with every check), which the result shows, check.json, sheet.png (a frame from each shot) and wave.png (the sound over time). A failed check is a normal result here. It knows no platform, and does not measure file size, codec, bitrate or the space an app's buttons cover. A launch film is {fact:launch-film.fps} frames a second and measures about {fact:launch-film.lufs} LUFS as it was rendered.

film.description: The video to check, like film.mp4. A launch-film timeline next to it under the same name, like film.timeline.json next to film.mp4, gives the cuts.

expect.description: The size and frame rate it should have, as WxH@fps, WxH or @fps: {fact:launch-film.size_16_9}@{fact:launch-film.fps} for a launch film ({fact:launch-film.size_9_16}@{fact:launch-film.fps} for 9:16), and for a demo its size at the fps it was recorded with.

seconds.description: The length it should have: 30 is give or take {fact:launch-film.check_seconds_tolerance} seconds, and a range like 28-32 takes anything inside it. A launch film's exact length is seconds in its film.timeline.json.

lufs.description: The integrated loudness it should have, like {fact:launch-film.lufs_social}, give or take {fact:launch-film.check_lufs_tolerance} LU. A launch film measures about {fact:launch-film.lufs} as it was rendered and nothing here changes that, so give a value only when the user needs that level.

cues.description: The cues.json of the music under the video, to check the cuts land on the beat. analyze_music writes one for a track played as it is. fit_music writes one for a fitted track. A track with no steady beat gives empty beats, which this refuses.

cuts.description: The cuts in seconds, like 3.2,7.5, or a JSON file of seconds, of frames with their fps, or a launch-film timeline, when no timeline of the video's own name is next to it: a renamed or mixed copy of a launch film takes its film.timeline.json here. A demo's steps.json is not one: give its clicks' pressedAt as seconds.

allow.description: Stretches meant to hold still, black or silent, in seconds, like 27-30,0-0.5.

passed: A measurement cannot read words: look at {file:sheet.png}, or give the user its path, for words cut off, text on text and a wrong logo before handing the video over.
check_failed: Read which checks failed in CHECK.md below.
For a launch film, a loudness or true peak failure is how it was rendered: tell the user the measurement instead of rendering again, and a frame rate of {fact:launch-film.fps} is the film's own.
A launch film planned with music false fails the silence check until a track is under it.
Then look at {file:sheet.png}, or give the user its path, since a measurement cannot read words.

Give the user the {name:sheet.png} link from the list below, since a measurement cannot read words.
